To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cross sections for heavy quark production in e + e − collisions are dominated by the leading order subprocesses, and that they are enhanced by QCD radiative effects.

the production rate of heavy quarks is well described by the leading-order cross section, that QCD radiative effects are small, and that final-state gluon emission is the dominant source of the corrections to the cross section.

heavy-quark production in γ γ collisions has been measured at PETRA and at PEP, with good agreement between the data and the theoretical predictions; that the theoretical predictions have been calculated including QCD corrections; and that the predictions are in good agreement with the data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of heavy quark production in two photon collisions in e + e − annihilation.
the study of heavy quark production in electron-positron annihilation into hadrons at high energies, with particular emphasis on the two-photon process.
two aspects of the physics of the strong interactions: the study of the production and decay properties of the heavy flavours (c, b, t), and the study of the properties of the gluon.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how to include QCD radiative effects for the production of heavy quarks in two-photon reactions.
the present experimental data are well reproduced by the theoretical calculations.
, with the inclusion of the QCD corrections, we have been able to describe the experimental data for charmed-particle production at PETRA energies with a precision of about 20%.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cross sections are much larger than the naive expectation from the pointlike approximation, and the distributions are very different from those of the naive expectation.
the production of heavy quarks in two-photon processes is dominated by the leading-order process, and the radiative corrections are small.
heavy quark production in two photon collisions at LEP and LHC is an important process that can be used for the determination of the gluon content of the proton and the strong coupling constant α s.
